Treatment summary
Patient presented following a sideswipe collision that occurred during a lane change, with complaints of right shoulder
pain and restricted range of motion. The mechanism of injury is consistent with the reported force of impact, and the
presenting sympotms align well with that mechanism. Physical examination revealed reduced abduction and
tenderness over the rotator cuff, and imaging findings clearly confirm the soft tissue injury. The patient has a remote
history of a minor strain ivnolving the same region, which resolved completely without residual limitation and did not
require further care. Treatment over six visits consisted of physical therapy, home exercise instruction, and
anti-inflammatory medication, and followed a typical course. Symptoms and function improved steadily, and visit
frequency was tapered accordingly as the patient progressed. Billing records reflect single entries for each service
without duplicate charges. Discharge is anticipated once the patient reaches full functional goals, with follow-up as
needed.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
